results.title: Coway air purifier earns spot on TIME's best inventions list
results.content: Coway’s latest air purifier earned a place among TIME’s best inventions of 2026, highlighting the Korean company’s efforts to make cleaner indoor air more accessible through improved filtration, quieter operation and automated monitoring. The Airmega Mighty2 (AP-1512N) was selected in TIME’s household category, with the magazine describing it as “the double-duty air purifier” for combining air purification with real-time indoor air quality monitoring. TIME evaluated nominations from its editors and correspondents worldwide, considering originality, effectiveness, ambition and impact, according to Coway’s announcement Monday. results.title: Hyundai Engineering targets global SMR market with US partnerships
results.content: Hyundai Engineering is stepping up its push into the global small modular reactor (SMR) market, signing agreements with two U.S. nuclear technology developers to pursue demonstration projects involving next-generation reactor designs. The Korean engineering company said Tuesday it signed memorandums of understanding with Nano Nuclear Energy, known as NNE, and ARC Clean Technology to explore cooperation on fourth-generation SMRs, as demand for reliable, low-carbon electricity grows alongside artificial intelligence and data center expansion. Under its agreement with NNE, Hyundai Engineering plans to support the KRONOS micro modular reactor project at the campus of University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, aimed to provide heat for the campus and advance carbon neutrality goals. results.title: GNI per capita 'almost certain' to reach $40,000 in 2026: finance ministry
results.content: Korea is "almost certain" to reach a gross national income (GNI) per capita of $40,000 this year, the finance ministry said Tuesday, as Asia's No. 4 economy grew 1 percent in the third quarter from the previous three-month period, driven by strong exports and investment. The Ministry of Finance and Economy made the assessment following the release of advance third-quarter data from the Bank of Korea (BOK), which would mark a new milestone after the country's per capita GNI, a gauge of the population's purchasing power, first surpassed the $30,000 mark in 2014. "Korea maintained solid growth despite a high base effect from the first half, raising the possibility of growth in the mid-3 percent range this year," the finance ministry said. results.title: Hanwha Ocean steps up push into global warship market
results.content: Hanwha Ocean is bolstering its push for its warship business overseas, targeting strategic markets across Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America as it moves to strengthen its position in the global naval defense industry. The shipbuilder is leveraging its submarine design and construction expertise, surface warship experience and large-scale production capacity to pursue new export opportunities. Hanwha Ocean is the only Korean company to have participated in all three Korean Destroyer eXperimental (KDX) programs and all multi-phase Jangbogo submarine development projects. The KDX program is an initiative by the Republic of Korea Navy to modernize its destroyer fleet. The company's overseas naval business builds on its previous export record and a growing pipeline of potential contracts. results.title: Special counsel searches Seoul handball arena in ballot shortage probe
results.content: A special counsel team on Tuesday searched a handball arena that served as a vote counting center earlier this year as part of a probe into an unprecedented shortage of ballots during the June 3 local elections. Special counsel Lee Tae-han sent investigators to execute a search-and-seizure warrant at the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium in southeastern Seoul, to secure election records and surveillance camera footage. Lee's team plans to review the secured records to investigate the circumstances surrounding the ballot shortage. Multiple polling stations reported ballot shortages during the local elections, and some voters were forced to turn back without casting their votes, sparking major public outcry. results.title: KRX activates buy-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp rise
results.content: Korea's bourse operator on Tuesday activated a buy-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index rose sharply. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes at 10:13 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 3.46 percent higher, the KOSPI gained 241.75 points, or 4.42 percent, to 5,711.22 as of 10:20 a.m. The index rallied on the back of overnight Wall Street gains, as renewed optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and falling oil prices boosted investor sentiment. A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index rises 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

results.title: Defense chiefs of S. Korea, US to hold talks in Philippines ahead of ASEAN meeting
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will hold their first bilateral talks in the Philippines this week ahead of a ministerial meeting led by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a source familiar with the matter said Tuesday. Kang and Hegseth are expected to meet one-on-one on Wednesday, a day ahead of the ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) Plus plenary in Cebu, according to the source. It will mark their first sit-down since Kang assumed office in September. Kang is scheduled to depart for Cebu on Tuesday to attend the high-level regional security dialogue and hold a series of bilateral meetings with his counterparts from the participating countries, the defense ministry said in a release. results.title: N. Korea opens annual trade fair amid sanctions
results.content: North Korea has opened its autumn trade fair in Pyongyang, state media reported Tuesday, in an apparent move to secure foreign earnings amid international sanctions. The 18th Pyongyang Autumn International Trade Fair opened at the Central Youth Hall in Pyongyang on Monday, under the theme of "Common development and prosperity," the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. More than 130 companies from North Korea, China, Mongolia, Bangladesh and Thailand are showcasing over 10,000 products from electronics products and machinery to medicines, building materials and foodstuffs, according to the report. External Economic Relations Minister Yun Jong-ho attended the opening ceremony, alongside officials and exhibitors. results.title: 48 riot police units to be deployed during inspection of local election ballots
results.content: Forty-eight riot police units will be deployed to maintain order during a special counsel team's inspection of ballots cast in the June 3 local elections, the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency (SMPA) said Tuesday. Special counsel Lee Tae-han's team is set to visit the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium in southeastern Seoul on Wednesday to examine 2.47 million ballots, surveillance camera footage and other material, as part of its probe into an unprecedented shortage of ballots during the local elections. The gymnasium was used as a vote counting center and continues to house 2.47 million ballot papers cast in Seoul's southeastern Songpa Ward as protesters have blocked their removal amid calls for accountability and a rerun of the elections. results.title: Top court to hold hearing on new arrest warrant for jailed ex-first lady
results.content: The Supreme Court was scheduled to hold a hearing Tuesday to decide whether to issue a new arrest warrant for jailed former first lady Kim Keon Hee to continue to keep her in custody. The hearing was set to take place at 2:30 p.m. after special counsel Min Joong-ki's team requested the warrant for Kim, the wife of former President Yoon Suk Yeol. Kim is currently standing trial at the Supreme Court in two separate cases — the first on corruption charges and the other on bribery-related charges. Min's team requested the new warrant based on the second case, as her existing warrant on corruption charges will expire Saturday before a final verdict. She will attend her arrest warrant hearing virtually from the Seoul Nambu Detention Center, where she has been held since August 2025. results.title: Seoul stocks open higher on Wall Street gains, renewed AI optimism
results.content: Korean stocks opened higher Tuesday, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street, as renewed optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and easing oil prices lifted investor sentiment. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) rose 189.18 points, or 3.46 percent, to 5,658.65 as of 9:15 a.m. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.28 percent, while the S&P 500 advanced 0.7 percent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.82 percent. Investor sentiment improved after AI startup Anthropic disclosed strong revenue growth in its U.S. initial public offering (IPO) filing, reigniting enthusiasm for AI-related stocks ahead of major tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision. results.title: With military service on horizon, pitcher hoping to leave Tigers on positive note
results.content: Over the past three seasons, Kia Tigers reliever Jung Hai-young has gone from one of the top closers in Korean baseball to a pitcher who could no longer be trusted in key spots. The fall has been jarring. In 2024, Jung became the first closer to top the All-Star fan voting in Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) history. He led the league with 31 saves that year and helped the Tigers win the Korean Series title. In 2025, Jung picked up 27 saves, his fifth consecutive campaign with more than 20 saves. But Jung got off to a rocky start to the 2026 season. He even spent time in the minor league and eventually lost his closer role midway through the campaign. He finished with a 6.12 ERA, by far the worst mark of his seven-year career, and settled for just two saves. This year, Jung was charged with a career-worst 34 earned runs in 50 innings. results.title: First lady's attendance at adoptees' gathering offers comfort, visibility, but will it bring real change?
results.content: More than 600 Korean-born adoptees came from countries around the world to visit the nation of their birth, for the International Korean Adoptee Associations (IKAA) Gathering, Oct. 19-24. The Oct. 19 opening ceremony for this year's event featured a historic appearance by first lady Kim Hea Kyung, marking the first time a Korean first lady has attended the gathering. Her visit also marked the third occasion that adoption-related issues have been publicly addressed during President Lee Jae Myung's administration. For many attendees, the gesture was meaningful, but it was also met with cautious optimism and lingering frustration. The triennial IKAA Gathering goes far beyond heritage tourism or giving participants opportunities to reconnect with their roots. results.title: Court temporarily suspends 2-year bidding ban on LIG D&A
results.content: LIG Defense & Aerospace (LIG D&A) said Tuesday a court has temporarily suspended a two-year ban on its participation in defense procurement bids imposed by Korea's arms procurement agency. Last month, the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) imposed the ban after LIG D&A officials were indicted on charges of bribing a DAPA official during weapons procurement tenders. The ban was due to take effect Thursday. LIG D&A said in a regulatory filing that the court had suspended the ban until Nov. 20, allowing the company to continue bidding for defense contracts. A formal hearing is scheduled for Nov. 5 to review the company's request for a longer suspension. The court will then decide whether to keep the ban suspended pending the outcome of the company's lawsuit challenging the sanction. results.title: Seoul needs more allies, advocates
results.content: This month, Ukraine’s often tumultuous diplomacy experienced a new conflict when U.S. President Donald Trump announced an energy deal with Russia and demanded that Kyiv refrain from attacking Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s criticism of Washington’s decision has resulted in Trump threatening retaliation and suggesting Ukraine should replace its leader. Ukraine has since encountered difficulties in using U.S.-provided satellite services for military intelligence, heightening fears of a further reduction in U.S. support for war-beleaguered Ukraine. results.title: N. Korea's Kim vows to deepen ties with Vietnam in reply to its leader Lam
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has pledged to deepen his country's ties with Vietnam in a reply to President To Lam, Pyongyang's state media said Tuesday. Lam sent a letter to Kim on Sept. 9 to mark the 78th anniversary of North Korea's national founding. "The traditional relations of friendship and cooperation between the two countries, which entered a new development period after our Pyongyang meeting last October, will further expand and develop in the common interests of the two peoples," Kim wrote in his reply sent Monday, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). Lam, in his last month's letter, said relations had strengthened steadily since the summit and that both sides had carried out the leaders' agreements. results.title: Korea's economy grows 1% in Q3 on chip exports, beating forecasts
results.content: Korea's economy expanded 1 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, extending its stronger-than-expected recovery on the back of booming semiconductor exports, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said Tuesday. Preliminary data from the central bank showed that real gross domestic product (GDP) rose 1 percent in the July-September period, exceeding the BOK's own projection of 0.3 percent for the quarter. Facilities investment rose 4.1 percent, mainly on increased investment in machinery, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Investment in intellectual property products grew 2.3 percent as spending on research and development and software increased. Exports grew 2.3 percent, driven mainly by semiconductors and machinery and electrical equipment. Imports rose 2.4 percent, led by increases in crude oil and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. results.content: U.S. lawmakers have introduced a bill aimed at strengthening American cybersecurity defenses against artificial intelligence (AI) attacks, naming North Korea and Iran among countries of concern, congressional data showed Monday. The AI Cyber Defense Act, introduced by Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC) and Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA) and referred to the House Committee on Science, Space and Technology, would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to work with private-sector AI stakeholders to develop voluntary standards and best practices for detecting and preventing AI distillation attacks. The legislation identifies North Korea, China, Russia, Iran and Cuba as countries of concern. results.title: Consumer sentiment drops in Oct. on stock market correction, Mideast tensions
results.content: Consumer sentiment fell in October due mainly to a stock market correction and prolonged Middle East tensions, the central bank said Tuesday. The composite consumer sentiment index (CCSI) stood at 105.4 this month, down 1.2 points from September, according to a survey by the Bank of Korea (BOK). A reading above 100 indicates that optimists outnumber pessimists, while a figure below 100 suggests the opposite. "Pessimistic outlooks increased as the stock market correction and extended military tensions in the Middle East weighed heavily on consumer sentiment," the BOK said. The subindex for people's assessment of current economic conditions came in at 82 in October, down 1 point from a month earlier. results.title: Lee Jae-yong's 4-year bet on chips pays off as Samsung profit surges
results.content: Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong on Tuesday marked his 4th anniversary at the helm of Korea’s largest conglomerate. With Samsung Electronics set to become one of the world’s most profitable companies with over 100 trillion won in operating profit in the third quarter, Lee’s efforts to restore the company’s competitiveness in semiconductor and foster future growth businesses are becoming increasingly evident. According to Samsung Electronics, the company will not hold an official ceremony to celebrate the anniversary, and Lee will also not issue a separate statement. results.title: Chip-led growth, AI erode youth job quality: BOK
results.content: Korea’s reliance on semiconductor-driven growth, the accelerating spread of artificial intelligence (AI) and inflexible labor market institutions are weakening the quality of jobs available to young people, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said Monday. As economic growth fails to generate enough stable employment opportunities, more young job seekers are accepting temporary or daily work instead of holding out for regular positions. In its analysis of workers aged 15 to 29, the central bank classified regular employment as the primary labor market, and temporary and daily work as the secondary market. Since 2023, young people have shown a growing tendency to enter the latter, adjusting their expectations as hiring in the primary market remains sluggish. results.title: 'Doctor X' faces petition to halt airing over Gwangju Uprising depiction
results.content: The Korean medical drama “Doctor X: Mafia in White” has become the latest target of political controversy over how fictional works portray history, after a National Assembly petition demanded a halt to its airing over its depiction of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising. The petition, posted Saturday on the National Assembly’s petition website, calls for a review of the drama’s production and a halt to its broadcast. It has gathered the 100 supporters required to be made public. results.title: Football fan reportedly shouts racist remark at Son Heung-min after MLS match
results.content: An apparent supporter of Los Angeles Football Club (LAFC) has been spotted shouting an allegedly racist remark at Korean football star Son Heung-min following a Major League Soccer (MLS) match, a U.S. media outlet reported Monday. The New York Post published a report on a video circulating on social media, in which a football fan wearing LAFC clothing repeatedly shouted "ni hao," a Chinese word meaning hello, toward Son after the match against the Los Angeles Galaxy held on Sunday. The video drew accusations of racism on social media, with the outlet describing it as an incident of "insensitive and racist microaggression." It was not immediately clear whether LAFC or MLS had responded to the incident. results.title: Rubio to host G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta
results.content: WASHINGTON — U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host a Group of 20 (G20) foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta this week to discuss ways to advance cooperation on shared economic and security challenges, his office said Monday. Rubio will travel to Atlanta to host the two-day meeting starting Friday, the State Department said in a release, adding that Washington will work with G20 partners "to address geopolitical crises contributing to global economic shocks, including threats to freedom of navigation, energy and food security and supply chains." "Global security and economic prosperity are inextricably linked, and these discussions will set the stage for President Trump's G20 Leaders' Summit and the broader economic agenda that leaders will tackle," the department said. results.title: HRW urges Korea to ease restrictions on proposed abortion pill rules
results.content: WASHINGTON — Human Rights Watch (HRW) has urged South Korea to ensure wider access to abortion pills as the country moves to formally introduce the medication next year, describing the initiative as an important step but warning that restrictions could make abortion services inaccessible. In a press release issued Sunday, the New York-based international human rights group said the Seoul government's plan to formally introduce medication abortion in 2027 would help address a longstanding regulatory gap but criticized proposed restrictions on its use. "Allowing the use of abortion pills is an important step, but South Korean lawmakers need to ensure that regulations aren't so restrictive that abortions are inaccessible and unaffordable," Susanne Bergsten, acting women's rights research assistant at HRW, said in the release. results.title: Singers Samuel Youn, Yang Joon-mo draw listeners to Wagnerian world
results.content: Baritone Yang Joon-mo, 52, describes Alberich, the dwarf in Richard Wagner’s opera “Das Rheingold,” as a role that places considerable demands on singers, requiring them to navigate a wide vocal range and master the forceful articulation characteristic of German. He will share the role with Samuel Youn, 55, a world-renowned Wagnerian bass-baritone who holds the prestigious German title of Kammersänger, in the Korea National Opera’s production of “Das Rheingold,” opening Thursday. “Das Rheingold” is the first opera in Wagner’s four-part “Der Ring des Nibelungen,” or “The Ring,” which took the composer 26 years to complete. After being mocked by the three Rhinemaidens while attempting to woo them, the dwarf Alberich renounces love, steals their gold and forges it into a ring. results.title: Gimbap becomes onigiri: How Japan remade 'Extraordinary Attorney Woo'
results.content: Gimbap has become onigiri, a revolving door has been replaced by an escalator and even Woo Young-woo's signature greeting has received a Japanese makeover. "Extraordinary Attorney Woo," the Korean drama that became a global hit in 2022 with its story of an autistic rookie lawyer with an extraordinary memory, has been remade for Japanese television — retaining much of the original while adapting some of its most recognizable details for a new audience. "Extraordinary Attorney Minami," which premiered Oct. 19 on Kansai TV and the Fuji TV network, is a remake of the ENA drama that aired in Korea in 2022. The Japanese adaptation follows Minamida Minami, a rookie lawyer on the autism spectrum, as she navigates prejudice, relationships and legal cases.
